environment.description: Quarkus 3.2 application deployed as AWS Lambda with the function URL auth type set to AWS_IAM (not NONE). The ONLY ingress path is through a CloudFront distribution configured with Origin Access Control (OAC) using SigV4 signing to the Lambda function URL. The CloudFront distribution has a custom cache behavior for /api/* with Trusted Key Group enforcement requiring Ed25519 signed URLs (Policy type, not Canned). The key group 'kg-prod-2024' contains a single public key with ID 'K2DJ8FQXYZ1234'. Direct Lambda function URL invocation returns 403 due to IAM auth requirement - only the CloudFront OAC role has lambda:InvokeFunctionUrl permission via resource-based policy. CloudFront viewer protocol policy is HTTPS-only. The signed URL policy restricts the resource pattern to '/api/search?q=*' with a 60-second expiry and IP address condition matching the client's /32 CIDR. An attacker cannot generate valid signed URLs without the private key corresponding to the trusted key group.

config.signed_url_policy: Custom policy, resource=/api/search?q=*, 60s TTL, IP /32 CIDR condition
config.direct_origin_access: blocked (IAM auth on function URL, only OAC role permitted)
